command: python -m certreq run vendor/industrial-ai-hackathon/cases/dev-rear-lamp --select llm --filters all --extract modal,llm --out out/E016-a.json

selection.reason: The rear-position, stop and reversing functions fall within its consolidated light-signalling-device requirements, including photometric performance, emitted colour and LED-module provisions.
The integrated PMMA prism retro-reflector must meet the applicable retro-reflector requirements for passive conspicuity.
Installation on the M1 car must satisfy requirements for the lamps and retro-reflector concerning number, position, orientation, geometric visibility and electrical operation.
The LED modules and PCB constitute an electrical/electronic assembly whose electromagnetic emissions and immunity must be addressed under the applicable component and vehicle EMC requirements.
The exposed lens, housing and attachment geometry form part of the M1 vehicle's exterior and must satisfy applicable external-projection requirements.
The stop-lamp function must be integrated with the M1 braking system's prescribed braking-signal generation and deactivation.
The rear lamp's placement and mounting must support the vehicle-level requirements for continued lighting and signalling operation and visibility after prescribed low-speed impacts.
Its rear-position and stop-lamp provisions are consolidated into selected UN R148, so it is not selected separately.
Its reversing-lamp provisions are consolidated into selected UN R148, so it is not selected separately.
Its retro-reflector provisions are consolidated into selected UN R150, so it is not selected separately.
PCB-mounted LED modules do not establish use of an Annex 1 standardized LED light-source category; the specified modules are addressed through the lamp approval under UN R148.
Its scope explicitly excludes glazing for lighting and light-signalling devices, including this lamp's PMMA outer lens.

note: AP2: --select llm + E014-Konfiguration (--filters all --extract modal,llm), Richter strict
